'''Brandon Xavier Ingram''' (born September 2, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is a two-time [[NBA All-Star]] and was named the [[NBA Most Improved Player]] in 2020. He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with the second overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]], and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in the same season.

Ingram had a successful high school career in [[North Carolina]], where he won state titles each of his four years, and was named [[North Carolina Mr. Basketball|North Carolina's Mr. Basketball]]. He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], where he was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|Atlantic Coast Conference Rookie of the Year]]. After the season, Ingram decided to forgo his remaining college eligibility and declared for the NBA draft. He played three seasons with the Lakers before being traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in 2019 as part of a package for All-Star [[Anthony Davis]].

==Early life==
Ingram was born on September 2, 1997, in [[Kinston, North Carolina]]. He is the son of Donald and Joann Ingram. He has two half-siblings, an older brother, Donovan, and an older sister, Brittany.<ref name="BIrareStar">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/dukes-brandon-ingram-is-rare-case-of-a-quiet-creative-superstar/|title=Duke's Brandon Ingram is rare case of a quiet, creative superstar|last=Norlander|first=Matt|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 16, 2016|access-date=November 8, 2016}}</ref> He shares a father with Donovan and a mother with Brittany.<ref name=BIrareStar/> Ingram's father started his career as a [[police officer]] and a manager of a local gym, but he is now full-time at a welding plant, where he makes [[forklift]]s.<ref name=BIrareStar/><ref name="abcRise">{{Cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/brandon-ingrams-rise-brought-batch-duke-fans/story?id=37911856|title=Brandon Ingram's rise has brought a whole new batch of Duke fans|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|last=McGee|first=Ryan|date=March 24, 2016|access-date=July 3, 2016}}</ref> Before that, Donald was a would-be hoops star, pushing his way through the semi-pro leagues.<ref name="abcRise"/> When he moved back home to Kinston, his father started playing pickup games with a young [[Jerry Stackhouse]], who was looking to play locally against older and more experienced players to help him elevate his game.<ref name="abcRise"/> Stackhouse, an ex-[[NBA]] star and Kinston native, forged a friendship with Ingram's father on the court.

While Ingram grew up in a one-story house on Highland Avenue in Kinston, his brother Donovan grew up in a different house but would spend weekends with Brandon, teaching him basketball.<ref name=BIrareStar/> Ingram was able  to keep a steady focus on basketball despite a high crime rate in the local community in Kinston. <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://heavy.com/sports/2016/06/brandon-ingram-family-parents-mom-dad-sister-brother-photos-pics-from-who/|title=Brandon Ingram's Family: The Pictures You Need to See|last=Adams|first=Jonathan |publisher=Heavy|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=November 8, 2016}}</ref> Before Ingram was a teenager, his brother allowed him to play with him and his older friends. He described this experience as "the best thing that ever happened to my game". His brother, known as Bo,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.utamavs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ingram_bo00.html|title=Bo Ingram Bio :: UTAMavs.com :: The Official Site of UT Arlington Mavericks Men's Basketball|access-date=March 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170309065236/http://www.utamavs.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ingram_bo00.html|archive-date=March 9, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> went on to play [[college basketball]] for [[South Plains College]] (2008–2010) and [[UT Arlington Mavericks men's basketball|UT Arlington]] (2010–2012).<ref name="goduke">{{Cite web |title=Brandon Ingram Bio |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/brandon-ingram/4400 |access-date=September 4, 2023 |website=goduke.com}}</ref> By the time Brandon reached eighth grade, Stackhouse became Ingram's [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) coach and mentored the young basketball player.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/articles/brandon-ingram-duke-goodbye-letter|title=Farewell, Duke {{!}} By Brandon Ingram|website=The Players' Tribune|access-date=April 18, 2016}}</ref> Those influences "took me to the next level", said Ingram, whose foundation as a player came from his father.<ref name="NBA-bound">{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/draft/2016/06/22/brandon-ingram-ben-simmons-mike-krzyzewski-nba-draft/86263068/|title=NBA-bound Brandon Ingram cool on the surface, fiery beneath it|last=Gleeson|first=Scott|work=[[USA Today]]|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=July 3, 2016}}</ref> His father was a high school and collegiate referee who stated Brandon "was trained correctly, both mentally and physically. He grew up knowing the rules of the game".<ref name="NBA-bound"/> Ingram played all four years of his high school basketball career at [[Kinston High School (North Carolina)|Kinston High School]] and helped lead Kinston to four straight state championships during his time there.<ref>[http://www.kinston.com/sports/local/brandon-ingram-is-the-free-press-player-of-the-year-1.460541?page=1 Brandon Ingram is The Free Press Player of the Year]</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2025–2026)===
On February 6, 2025, Ingram was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for guard-forward [[Bruce Brown (basketball)|Bruce Brown]], center [[Kelly Olynyk]], a 2026 first-round draft pick (via Indiana) and a 2031 second-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 6, 2025 |title=RAPTORS ACQUIRE INGRAM FROM NEW ORLEANS |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-acquire-ingram-from-new-orleans |access-date=September 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 12, he signed a 3-year, $120 million contract extension with the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=RAPTORS EXTEND INGRAM |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-extend-ingram |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 4, 2025 |date=February 12, 2025}}</ref> On April 9, before ever being able to suit up for the franchise, he was officially shut down for the season following a [[Platelet-rich plasma|PRP injection]] in his ankle to aid in his recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 9, 2025 |title=Raptors' Brandon Ingram gets injection for ankle, season over |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44607917 |access-date=September 27, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On November 13, 2025, Ingram was fined $25,000 by the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] for an incident during a game against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. After being called for a [[Foul (basketball)|foul]], he was subbed out. He threw a water bottle to the floor, which accidentally hit a game attendant and Ingram was assessed for a [[technical foul]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Raptors star receives huge fine from the NBA |url=https://basketnews.com/news-234780-raptors-star-receives-huge-fine-from-the-nba.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=13 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

On February 10, 2026, Ingram was named as an All-Star for the second time in his career, replacing the injured [[Stephen Curry]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Sportsnet |date=2026-02-10 |title=Raptors' Brandon Ingram to replace Steph Curry at 2026 NBA All-Star Game |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-brandon-ingram-to-replace-steph-curry-in-2026-nba-all-star-game/ |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=Sportsnet.ca |language=en}}</ref>

During the second quarter of Game 5 on April 29, 2026, Ingram re-aggravated a right heel injury and was forced to exit the game after playing only 11 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Collier |first=Jamal |date=April 29, 2026 |title=Raptors' Brandon Ingram (heel) exits Game 5 loss to Cavaliers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48632845/raptors-brandon-ingram-exits-game-5-vs-cavs-heel-injury |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref> On May 8, 2026, Ingram underwent right heel surgery.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brandon Ingram undergoes surgery |url=https://basketnews.com/news-246996-brandon-ingram-undergoes-surgery.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=11 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

On July 2nd, 2026, Toronto agreed to trade Ingram, Gradey Dick, their 2031 and 2033 1st round picks, 2030 and 2033 2nd round picks, and a 2027 1st round pick swap to the Los Angeles Clippers in exchange for Kawhi Leonard. However, due to the NBA's investigation into Leonard and the Clippers for salary cap circumvention, the trade has yet to be processed. 

==National team career==
Ingram was selected to the 2016 [[United States men's national basketball team#Select Team|U.S. select team]], which trained with the [[2016 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2016 U.S. Olympic basketball team]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/06/2016-usa-mens-select-team.aspx | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160609233301/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/06/2016-usa-mens-select-team.aspx | url-status=dead | archive-date=June 9, 2016 | title=USA Basketball Names 25 Top Young NBA Players To 2016 USA Men's Select Team | publisher=[[USA Basketball]] | date=June 7, 2016 | access-date=June 27, 2016}}</ref> He was also a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] that competed in the [[2023 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], finishing fourth overall.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-11 |title=Team USA Grades: How every American player fared in disappointing FIBA World Cup showing |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/team-usa-grades-how-every-american-player-fared-in-disappointing-fiba-world-cup-showing/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Player profile==
[[File:20150329 MCDAAG closed practice Brandon Ingram (3).JPG|thumb|right|upright|Ingram during a closed practice of the 2015 [[McDonald's All-American Game]]]]

Ingram is a {{convert|6|ft|8|in}}, prototypical modern wing scorer with size and feel.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Ingram|website=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/brandon_ingram|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191028063238/https://www.nba.com/players/brandon/ingram/1627742|archive-date=October 28, 2019}}</ref> Since joining the Raptors, he has consistently been one of the primary offensive options, averaging around 21-22 points per game while showing efficient scoring across multiple levels. His size and shooting touch allow him to shoot over defenders, hit jumpers, and create tough buckets in isolation or when the offense stalls. Ingram’s length and craft give him upside defensively, though that end remains an area of fluctuation. He adds secondary playmaking to the Raptors’ offense alongside Scottie Barnes and provides scoring gravity that helps open looks for others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/how-brandon-ingram-has-catalyzed-raptors-offensive-surge/|title=How Brandon Ingram has catalyzed Raptors' offensive surge|last=Finlayson|first=Ian|publisher=[[Sportsnet]]|date=November 25, 2025|access-date=February 1, 2026}}</ref>

Over the years, Ingram has drawn frequent comparisons to [[Kevin Durant]], after whom he patterned his playing style revealing, "I try to take bits and pieces out of [Durant's] game and put it in my game [but] at the end of the day, he's Kevin Durant, and I'm Brandon Ingram".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2016/6/23/12014946/la-lakers-draft-news-brandon-ingram-kevin-durant|title=Lakers draft news: Brandon Ingram says he sees the comparisons between himself and Kevin Durant|last=Faigen|first=Harrison|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=July 25, 2016}}</ref> After a [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]] practice, Durant told reporters that Ingram is "the first person that I could... look at him and feel like I'm looking in the mirror".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uproxx.com/dimemag/kevin-durant-brandon-ingram-comparison-mirror/|title=High Praise As Kevin Durant Declares Brandon Ingram Is 'Like I'm Looking In A Mirror'|last=Rothstein|first=Matthew|publisher=[[Uproxx]]|date=June 20, 2016|access-date=July 25, 2016}}</ref>
